chunks: And We blessed him and Isaac. Among their descendants are some who do good, but some who wrong themselves.

key_terms.إِسْحَاقَ: Isaac, son of Jacob, a key prophet in Islamic tradition
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا: Their descendants, referring to the progeny of Jacob and Isaac
key_terms.ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ: One who wrongs himself, i.e., commits sin or injustice against his own soul
key_terms.مُحْسِنٌ: One who does good or is righteous

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the descendants of Jacob and Isaac regarding righteousness and sin?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah As-Saffat, this verse follows the narrative of Prophet Jacob (Ya'qub) and Isaac (Isaac), emphasizing that divine favor does not guarantee uniform piety among descendants. Shia scholarship often highlights this distinction to illustrate the principle of individual accountability, where the 'muhsin' (doer of good) and the 'zalim' (one who wrongs himself) represent the divergent spiritual paths available even within a blessed prophetic lineage.
